lane_views_hash_check.encoding: sha256 of json.dumps(view_ids in file order, separators=(',',':')) - NOT the schema-v1 newline-joined sorted encoding; raw schema-v1 hashes recomputed by verify.py are in per_scene

size_summary.note: Package files live on the fal volume (/data/splat-fal), not on this host; byte counts verified only as the sum of the per-file sizes recorded with sha256 in rows.jsonl. Parent 'bytes' is a float32 payload estimate, not a file.

control_check.reading: plain and QAT arms share fresh-Adam 3k continuation from the same parent, the same SH 4/3 codec and package format; they differ only in qat=True. The plain 3k float model is at or above the parent, and its 4/3 decode loses about as much as the parent encoded at 4/3 (spz43-overflow), so the control is a genuine decoded plain fine-tune. The +1.3 dB is QAT recovering aggressive SH4/3 quantization loss; against the default SPZ 6/6 of the same plain fine-tune (plain-spz66, ~1.55x larger) QAT is not compared by this rule.

decision_rule.rule: PASS iff mean PSNR loss (QAT-decoded - parent) <= 0.2 dB AND QAT beats plain-3k-decoded on >= 7/9

verdict.reason: recompute reproduces lane; 9 arms x 9 scenes N/N with identical views_hash; control verified; rule met

context_pubs.note: The extra 3k steps alone add ~+0.25 dB (plain float vs parent), so relative to its own fine-tuned float model QAT-decoded gives up ~0.27 dB. The same plain fine-tune at default SPZ 6/6 (plain-spz66) is ~0.15 dB above QAT-decoded at ~1.55x the bytes. Neither affects the registered rule (vs parent, and vs plain-3k at the same 4/3 codec); report both in the footnote.
